Fabric Selection By Exposure

Solar orientation dictates the daily thermal intake and brightness levels across every room. At In the Shade, we examine shifting daylight patterns alongside evening privacy needs for each window opening, so every pane pairs with an appropriate textile build. South-facing and west-facing exposures endure intense solar radiation during the late afternoon, which drives up air-conditioning runtimes. Fitting high-exposure glass with a honeycomb cellular design adds an insulating layer of trapped air directly against the pane, curbing heat transfer and easing cooling strain during peak outdoor temperatures.

Different compass points call for distinct illumination strategies. East-facing rooms receive intense morning glare that benefits from softening rather than full darkness, while north-facing openings receive muted, indirect daylight all afternoon and need minimal shading to keep clear outside views.
